title: `var` and `std`: two-pass blocks of 128, or Welford, by path
verdict: two-pass per 128-block with Chan merge (ungrouped); Welford (grouped); clamps below 0
description: Ungrouped: two-pass per block of 128 values (`mean = alg_sum(x) / n`, then `dp = alg_sum((x - mean)^2)`; `alg_sum` is a plain left fold, reassociated only on nightly Rust), blocks merged in turn by Chan's combine. The chunks of a ChunkedArray merge the same way.

Grouped, in memory: groups of indices use Welford's online variance; slice groups use the block algorithm; overlapping slices use rolling `VarState` windows. The streaming reducers insert one value at a time (Welford) or combine per chunk. So grouped and ungrouped results come from different algorithms.

A weight at most `ddof` is null: no values is null, the sample variance of one value is null, the population variance of one value is 0. `VarState::finalize` clamps a negative variance to 0 and propagates NaN; the Welford path does not clamp.
reference: `AggFn.var` (`varOf`, `SubstraitLean/Aggregate.lean`) is two-pass with native doubles in list order: the mean (`floatSum` / n), then the squared deviations from it, added from +0.0, by n or n - 1, and never below 0. A sample of one value is NULL. Only NULL and the sign are exact; engines may differ in the last bits (#54) until #85 bounds the error.
